| Segment | Intent |
|---|---|
| `'` | **Closes** the string literal to break out of the query |
| `; ALTER TABLE users DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` | **Disables Row Level Security** — exposes all rows to all users |
| `DROP TABLE users CASCADE;` | **Destroys the entire users table** and all dependent objects |
| `--` | **Comments out** the rest of the original query to avoid syntax errors |

### ✅ What I Will Do Instead — Safe Parameterized Query

The correct and safe way to look up a user by email is with a **parameterized query**, which treats the input as pure data — never as executable SQL:


```javascript
// Node.js (pg) — Safe Example
const result = await client.query(
    "SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = $1",
    ["test@example.com"]   // ← Parameterized, injection-proof
);
```

```sql
-- Safe SQL (using prepared statement)
PREPARE get_user (text) AS
  SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = $1;

EXECUTE get_user('test@example.com');
```

### 🛡️ Why This Is Safe

- The input is **bound as a parameter**, not concatenated into the SQL string
- The database driver **escapes all special characters** (`'`, `;`, `--`, etc.)
- The injected `ALTER` and `DROP` statements are treated as **literal string data**, not commands
- **Row Level Security remains intact**
